assumptions_made: Used the synthetic dataset from gretelai/synthetic_text_to_sql if it contained numeric features suitable for clustering
When the synthetic dataset was unsuitable, fell back to generating synthetic point clouds with make_blobs
Generated three Gaussian blobs in two dimensions with configurable separation
Used the same number of clusters (3) for both k-means and random assignment
Tested three separation levels: 0.5 (low overlap), 1.0 (medium overlap), and 2.0 (high overlap)
Applied StandardScaler to normalize features when using the synthetic dataset
Used the same random seed for reproducibility across experiments
Used Adjusted Rand Index as the primary metric for comparing clustering quality
Used within-cluster inertia as a secondary measure of clustering quality
Implemented proper error handling for cases where the synthetic dataset is unavailable or unsuitable

results.hypothesis: Test whether k-means recovers known cluster structure better than random assignment at increasing overlap.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Random assignment of points to the same number of clusters.
results.success_criteria: k-means beats random assignment on adjusted Rand index at every separation level tested.
results.notes: K-means ARI: 0.420, Random ARI: 0.002. K-means performs better.
